title: Minimum Number of Moves to Seat Everyone
summary: Given an array of seat positions and an array of student positions, determine the least number of moves needed to seat each student in a seat, ensuring no two students occupy the same seat.
statement: Given an array of seat positions and an array of student positions, determine the least number of moves needed to seat each student in a seat, ensuring no two students occupy the same seat. Moves involve shifting a student's position by one seat to the left or right.
constraints: seats and students have equal length up to 100 with integer positions.
Moving one student one position costs one move; every seat receives exactly one student.
hints: On a line, crossing two assignments can be uncrossed without increasing total distance.
Sort both position lists and pair them by rank.
The exchange inequality |a-d|+|b-c| >= |a-c|+|b-d| for a<=b and c<=d removes crossings until the sorted matching remains.
editorial: The exchange inequality |a-d|+|b-c| >= |a-c|+|b-d| for a<=b and c<=d removes crossings until the sorted matching remains.

tests.explanation: After sorting, the paired distances are one, one, and two, totaling four.
Sorted order matching gives total moves seven.
